holidays.name: National Devil's Food Cake Day
holidays.description: Today is for a slice of the chocolatey, fudgy cake with a wicked name. Devil's food cake is dark, moist and rich. It's usually layered with fluffy frosting or glossy ganache.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance, and nobody has traced it to a single founder. The cake dates to early 20th-century America. It got its name as the cheeky opposite of pale, airy angel food cake.
holidays.funFact: Early devil's food recipes often used a lot of cocoa and baking soda. The baking soda reacts with the cocoa and gives the cake a reddish tint.

holidays.name: Plant Something Day
holidays.description: Today's task is to put something in the ground. It could be a tree, a tomato seedling, a flower or a pot of herbs on the windowsill. It's a reminder that anyone can be a gardener.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's popular with gardeners who use it as an excuse to start spring planting.
holidays.funFact: Herbs like basil and mint are among the easiest plants to start with. Mint grows so aggressively that gardeners often keep it in its own pot.

holidays.name: Stepmother's Day
holidays.description: Today is a day to thank the women who step into a family and help raise kids who aren't biologically theirs. It's a chance to give some love to stepmoms, who are often overlooked.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's been observed on May 19 in the United States, and it falls close to Mother's Day.
holidays.funFact: Fairy tales gave stepmothers a bad reputation, with Cinderella as the best-known example. Stepmother's Day is a way to push back on that old stereotype.
